correctness.rationale: Exact independent rational matrix arithmetic verifies the complete hypotheses: T=diag(2,1), U=[[2,1],[1,1]] positive invertible, A1=(1/10)[[1,1],[1,1]] and A2=[[2/5,-1/10],[-1/10,9/10]] positive, with A1+A2=T^{-1}. Taking Lambda_i=A_i^(1/2), the two-atom controlled energy is <T(A1+A2)Uf,f>=<Uf,f>, with strictly positive bounds (3+-sqrt(5))/2. Yet M1=T A1 U=[[3/5,2/5],[3/10,1/5]] is nonsymmetric and its quadratic value at (-3,5) is exactly -1/10, so it is not positive and has no positive self-adjoint square root of the kind the source requires. The counterexample leaves the aggregate frame operator U well defined. With additional pointwise M_x>=0 and strong square-root field measurability, Jf(x)=v(x)M_x^(1/2)f is bounded by sqrt(B); this is sufficient, not asserted necessary. This checks the precise theorem hypothesis and square-root step rather than confusing algebraic square roots with positive roots.
correctness.risk: One must distinguish a positive self-adjoint square root from an arbitrary algebraic square root of an operator.

final_claim: The pointwise positive-square-root coefficient field used in Proposition 3.3 and Theorem 3.4 of Ghosh–Samanta (arXiv:2110.11234) need not exist for a genuine continuous controlled \(g\)-fusion frame: positive aggregate controlled energy does not imply that each mixed coefficient operator is self-adjoint positive. The exact real two-atom example proves failure; pointwise positivity plus measurability suffices for the specified coefficient construction.
limitations: Only the positive-square-root coefficient representation is refuted; the global frame operator remains positive.
The sufficiency repair also requires measurability of the square-root field and is not asserted optimal.
The example is in real two-dimensional Hilbert space with counting measure, as permitted by the source.
